newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian spot natural gas unchanged in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natural gas unchanged in light trade.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were unchanged in very light trade on Friday as the combination of the U.S. Independence Day Holiday and start of the Calgary Stampede festival brought action to a near halt, traders said.

Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub for weekend delivery was quoted at C$1.49 per gigajoule, the same as Thursday. The spot transport charge to Empress on the Alberta-Saskatchewan border from AECO remained at a deeply discounted 1-2 cents.
"Not many people are working in Calgary. The market is very illiquid," a local trader said.
The annual 10-day Stampede is traditionally a very slow time in the Canadian gas trade, with staff at producing and marketing companies turning their attentions to western-style revelry.
Export markets were even quieter, after most U.S. buyers locked in weekend deals on Thursday ahead of today's Independence Day holiday, traders said.
Sumas, Wash. gas was pegged at an unchanged US$0.99/1.04 per million British thermal units and Niagara was talked at US$2.265/2.27 per mmBtu, although no trades were reported midway through Friday.
The Canadian Gas Association earlier reported that gas in storage at June 27 across the country was at 36.3 percent of capacity, down slightly from 39 percent last year.

In the east, stocks were at 29.2 percent of capacity, up from 28.9 percent a year ago. Western facilites were 42.8 percent full compared to 47.4 at the same time in 1996, CGA said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
